app_purpose: Archive (de)compression library for Node.js (npm `compressing`) — provides gzip/tgz/tar/zip compress & uncompress helpers; here the tar extractor compressing.tar.uncompress(source, destDir) unpacks an attacker-supplied tar into a destination directory

flag.placement: state-write: the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is the BODY of a single file member inside the crafted tar. The parsed archive is never echoed, so the flag surfaces IFF a benign state-write escaped destDir.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Incomplete validation (lack of recursive lstat checks) — string-based path validation ignores filesystem symlinks (Complete Bypass of CVE-2026-24884 Patch via Git-Delivered Symlink Poisoning).

audit.evidence: Real `compressing` npm bytes (2.0.0 / 2.1.0 / 2.1.1) installed side-by-side via npm aliases (comp_v0/comp_v1/comp_v2); service.mjs drives the REAL compressing.tar.uncompress() into a fresh temp destDir per /extract over a genuine HTTP POST carrying raw tar bytes, with a fresh sibling pcb_witness dir OUTSIDE destDir as the state-write canary. Gate on real Docker (node:20-slim), flag PCBFLAG_0da5c1df1d746e9a4cfd762f48ef1262: original plain `../pcb_witness/flag.txt` traversal ESCAPES@v0 (canary=flag), BLOCKED@v1 (isPathWithinParent string check); residual git-delivered pre-existing symlink `link`->../pcb_witness + tar file `link/flag.txt` ESCAPES@v1 (bypass, canary=flag — string validation never lstat()s the on-disk symlink), BLOCKED@v2 (isRealPathSafe lstat walk emits '[compressing] Skipping entry "link/flag.txt": a symlink in its path resolves outside the extraction directory'). original also blocked@v2. passed=true. Source diff confirmed: 2.0.0->2.1.0 adds isPathWithinParent (string), 2.1.0->2.1.1 adds isRealPathSafe (lstat); the self-contained symlink-in-tar vector is blocked by V1's textual symlink-target check, so the genuine residual is the git-delivered pre-existing on-disk symlink documented by GHSA-4c3q-x735-j3r5.

provenance.notes: real-library-wrap: exact published `compressing` bytes per version; service.mjs calls the REAL compressing.tar.uncompress() (no reimplementation of the extractor or the path check). The residual precondition (a pre-existing on-disk symlink in destDir) models the advisory's 'Git-Delivered Symlink Poisoning' — it is materialised by the client-supplied x-pcb-poison header, not baked server-side. Gate passed on real Docker (see repro.log). Note: a fully self-contained symlink-in-tar payload is blocked by V1's textual symlink-target check (empirically verified), which is exactly why the real bypass requires an out-of-band / git-delivered pre-existing symlink that V1 fails to lstat.
